title: fix(rest): resolve the public-lookup picker target from the canonical `reference` (#7486)
body:
Fixes #7486

## The defect

`GET /forms/:slug/lookup/:field` presents `publicPicker.object` as an **optional** override — omit it and the server is supposed to resolve the target from the field's own definition on the parent object. It could not. The fallback chain read three **legacy** spellings only:

```ts
referenceTo = def?.referenceTo ?? def?.target ?? def?.options?.objectName;
```

while `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts:450` folds `relatedTo` / `referenceTo` / `target` / `targetObject` / `lookupObject` **all onto `reference`** at parse. A parsed, canonical object schema therefore carried **none** of the three keys the route read: the chain resolved `undefined` and the route answered `500 LOOKUP_TARGET_MISSING` for exactly the well-formed metadata the platform produces.

Net effect: `publicPicker.object` was de-facto **required**, while the schema and the docs presented it as optional.

## The fix

`def?.reference` now heads the chain. The legacy spellings are kept **after** it, not replaced — rows stored before the alias fold never went through the alias table and still carry them, so this **widens** the resolution rather than moving it.

Precedence: `reference` → `referenceTo` → `target` → `options.objectName`.

⛔ **No spec change.** The spec was right; the consumer was reading the wrong keys.

## Tests

`packages/rest/src/public-form-lookup-picker.test.ts` (from #7467) declared `object` explicitly **because of this bug**, so it only ever exercised the override branch — leaving the fix unguarded at the level users actually hit. It is **extended**, not left as-is: the #7467/#7485 suites keep the override branch, and a new `#7486` suite covers the omitted-`object` branch. Every case there omits `object` deliberately; that is the axis under test.

| Case | Pins |
|---|---|
| a canonical `{ type: 'lookup', reference: 'sys_user' }` field resolves with no `object` override | the headline case — `500` before this change |
| the three legacy spellings (`referenceTo`, `target`, `options.objectName`) still resolve | stored pre-fold rows, the reason they stay in the chain |
| `reference` **wins** over a legacy spelling on the same def | head-of-chain, not merely present-in-chain |
| GUARD: a def naming no target at all **still** answers `500 LOOKUP_TARGET_MISSING` | the error became rare, not unreachable |

### Mutation table — each new test proved able to fail

| Mutant | Red |
|---|---|
| pre-fix chain (drop the `reference` head) | canonical case · precedence case (2 failed / 10 passed) |
| `reference` appended at the **tail** of the chain | precedence case (1 failed / 11 passed) |
| chain **replaced** by `def?.reference` (legacy dropped) | all three legacy-spelling cases (3 failed / 9 passed) |
| guard defeated (`?? match.object` appended) | the `LOOKUP_TARGET_MISSING` guard (1 failed / 11 passed) |
| baseline restored | 12 passed |

## Docs

`content/docs/ui/forms.mdx` described the defect as if it were the design: its error table pointed authors hitting `LOOKUP_TARGET_MISSING` at "declare `publicPicker.object`". That row and the `object` key row are corrected in the same change — the override is now genuinely optional, and the 500 row names what actually causes it.

⛔ No `content/docs/releases/**` edits. A changeset (`@objectstack/rest` patch) is included.

## Checks

- `pnpm lint` — clean
- `pnpm typecheck` — 126/126 tasks
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test` — 84 files / 1360 tests pass (re-run after merging `origin/main` @ `d063a96` and rebuilding)

Scope respected: only the public-forms lookup handler region of `rest-server.ts` is touched — `mapDataError` (#7525), `/meta` route registration (#7526) and the reports-delete region are untouched.
